title: Chile Chicken and Bean Guisado (UNTESTED)
headnote: UNTESTED — not yet cooked or rated by the cookbook owner. A quick Mexican-inspired ground-chicken and white-bean stew by Kristina Felix (NYT Cooking); approximately 35 minutes, 4 servings. Reconstructed from published recipe information. This is a cook-ready draft, not a confirmed family favorite.

ingredientGroups.title: Chicken and aromatics
items: Kosher salt, to taste (start with about 1 tsp Diamond Crystal)

ingredientGroups.title: Seasoning and stew
items: 2 tsp ancho chile powder (or chipotle chile powder for more heat)
2 × 425 g cans white beans (can weight before draining), drained and rinsed
475 g low-sodium chicken broth (2 cups; approximate)

steps: Heat the avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, around 3 minutes.
Add the ground chicken and a little kosher salt. Break it into small pieces while it cooks; continue until no longer pink, about 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, vinegar, ancho chile powder, oregano, and cinnamon. Cook briefly, about 2 minutes, to release their aroma.
Add the rinsed white beans, chicken broth, and diced tomatoes. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
If using spinach or arugula, add near the end and cook just until wilted. Ensure the chicken is fully cooked to 165°F. Taste and adjust salt and acidity.
Serve with warm tortillas and optional salsa roja, cilantro, and diced onion. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
